parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἀγορά (agorá).

parole.significato: alpha; the Greek letter Α, α
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἄλφα (álpha).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آولی (avlı, “courtyard”), from Ancient Greek αὐλή (aulḗ).
Borrowed from Ancient Greek ἀζαλέος (azaléos, “dry”), because the plant grows in dry soil.
Ultimately from Ancient Greek βάρος (báros, “weight”).

parole.significato: threshing sledge, a rectangular wooden plank designed to separate grain from chaff
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish دوگن (döğen, düğen, döven, düven), itself from a variant of Ancient Greek τυκάνη (tukánē, “threshing instrument”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فانطازیه (fantazya), from Ancient Greek φαντασία (phantasía). Doublet of fantezi.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فنار (fenar, fener, “lantern; lighthouse”), from Old Anatolian Turkish فنار (fänār), ultimately from Ancient Greek φανάριον (phanárion).

parole.significato: basil, sweet basil, any culinary herb of the species Ocimum basilicum
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فسلكن (fesleğen), from Ancient Greek βασιλικόν (basilikón).
From Ancient Greek ἡγεμονία (hēgemonía).
From Ottoman Turkish هلیك (helik), from a form of Ancient Greek χᾰ́λῐξ (khắlĭx). Compare modern Greek χαλίκι (chalíki).
Ultimately from Ancient Greek ὁμός (homós, “one and the same, common, joint”), from Proto-Indo-European *somHós. Doublet of hem.

From Ottoman Turkish خلیا, خولیا (hulya), from Ancient Greek χολία (kholía), from χολή (kholḗ, “bile”), from Proto-Hellenic *kʰolā́, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰolh₃-éh₂, from *ǵʰelh₃- (“green, yellow”).

parole.significato: felloe, felly, the outer rim of a wooden wheel, supported by the spokes
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اسپید (ispid), metathesized form of اپسد (ipsid, “felloe”), itself from Ancient Greek ἁψῑ́ς (hapsī́s, “wheel, hoop”).
From Ottoman Turkish ازماریت (izmarit), from Ancient Greek σμαρίς (smarís), which possibly has a pre-Greek origin.

parole.significato: hump, hunch, a deformity in humans caused by an abnormal curvature of the upper spine
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قنبور (kanbur, “hump, hunch”), possibly from Ancient Greek καμπύλος (kampúlos, “bent, curved”) from κάμπτω (kámptō, “to bend, curve”).

parole.significato: centaury, any flowering plant in the genus Centaurium
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قنطارون (kantaron), ultimately from Ancient Greek κενταύριον (kentaúrion).
From Ottoman Turkish كیانوس (kiyanus), from Ancient Greek κῠ́ᾰνος (kŭ́ănos, “dark-blue enamel”); doublet of siyanojen and siyanür.
From Ottoman Turkish كورفز, ultimately from Ancient Greek κόλπος (kólpos, “gulf, bay, creek”). Cognate with English gulf.
From Ottoman Turkish كومس (kümes) from Ancient Greek Koıμασιον (Koımasion, “sleeping place”).

parole.significato: cogon, cogon grass, satintail, any of several perennial grasses of the genus Imperata, especially Imperata cylindrica
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قندره (kandara) or قندری (kandarı), which according to Nishanyan derives from Ancient Greek καλαμανθήλη (kalamanthḗlē).
From Ottoman Turkish لامبه (lamba), لامپه (lampa), from Ancient Greek λαμπάς (lampás, “lamp”), from Ancient Greek λάμπω (lámpō, “shine”).
From Ottoman Turkish لودوس (lodos), from Ancient Greek νότος (nótos, “wind from the South”).
Ottoman Turkish مداره (madara), Nişanyan suggests it is borrowed from Ancient Greek μαδαρός (madarós, “bald, moist”). TDK suggests it is borrowed from Persian مدر
From Ottoman Turkish مطرباز (madrabaz, matrabaz), from Ancient Greek μεταπράτης (metaprátēs), equivalent to μετά (metá) + πιπράσκω/πέρνημι (pipráskō/pérnēmi)
From Ottoman Turkish ماندال (mandal), from Ancient Greek μάνδαλος (mándalos).

parole.significato: dairy farm, a place where dairy farming is practiced and dairy cattle is held
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ماندره (mandra), from Ancient Greek μᾰ́νδρᾱ (mắndrā, “cattle barn”).
From Ancient Greek μέγας (mégas, “great, large, mighty”).

parole.significato: A traditional Turkish breakfast dish of scrambled eggs cooked with diced tomatoes and green peppers, similar to North A…
parole.testo: The etymology remains unknown. Nişanyan disregards any relation with the placename Menemen and proposes that it's ultimately derived from or related to Ancient Greek μάλαγμα (málagma, “emollient, cataplasm; padding”). Modern Greek μενεμέν (menemén) is a borrowing from Turkish.

parole.significato: any mechanical appliance for exerting pressure or secure objects, such as a vise, a clamp, a press, etc.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish منكنه (mengene, “press, mangle”), from Ancient Greek μάγγανον (mánganon, “bolt; catapult; block of a pulley”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مرمر (mermer), from Ancient Greek μάρμαρος (mármaros, “marble”). Compare Marmara Denizi (“Sea of Marmara”), from the same word.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مدللی (midilli), from Ancient Greek Μῠτῐλήνη (Mŭtĭlḗnē).
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek μικρο- (mikro-).
Compare English microbiota and French microbiote, both from Ancient Greek roots.

parole.significato: grouper, any of various large fish of the subfamily Epinephelinae, specifically Epinephelus marginatus
parole.testo: Ultimately from Ancient Greek ὀρφώς (orphṓs, “dusky grouper”).

parole.significato: shingle, a thin board used as a covering for the roof
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پداوره (pedavra, padavra, “shingle”), ultimately from Ancient Greek πέταυρον (pétauron), variant of πέτευρον (péteuron, “springboard; platform, stage”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish [Term?], from Ancient Greek πῶλος (pôlos).
From Ancient Greek παλίνδρομος (palíndromos).

parole.significato: kind of two-oared boat similar to a gondola, used to carry cargo in the Aegean and Marmara seas
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پرامه (prama, prame), itself from Ancient Greek πέρᾱμᾰ (pérāmă, “ferry”).

parole.significato: the general name given to several plants of the families Ericaceae and Hypericaceae
parole.testo: Ultimately from Ancient Greek πρῖνος (prînos, “holm oak, ilex”).
Borrowed from Ancient Greek kυκλώνας (kuklṓnas, “cyclone”).
From Ottoman Turkish سلندر, ultimately from Ancient Greek κύλινδρος (kúlindros, “cylinder”), likely through French cylindre.
Internationalism from Ancient Greek σύναψις (súnapsis). See French synapse, English synapse.

From Ottoman Turkish سنور (sinor, sınor), from Old Anatolian Turkish سنور (sinor), from Ancient Greek σύνορον (súnoron, “frontier, border”), partly from Proto-Hellenic *wórwos, from Proto-Indo-European *werw-.

parole.significato: tachyon, a hypothetical particle thought to move faster than light
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek τάχυον (tákhuon).

parole.significato: lupin, any herbaceous, perennial plant of the genus Lupinus and its bean
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ترمیه (termiye, “lupin”), ultimately from Ancient Greek θερμός (thermós, “lupin”).

parole.significato: vault, an arched masonry structure supporting and forming a ceiling
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طولوس (tolos, “vault”), from Ancient Greek θόλος (thólos, “rotunda; vault”).
Ultimately from Ancient Greek τοπογραφία (topographía).

parole.significato: bow pin, a vertical pin attached to the yoke and hanging down from both sides of the animal's neck, to prevent it from…
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زلوه (zelve), ultimately from Ancient Greek ζεύγλη (zeúglē, “loop attached to the yoke”).

parole.significato: canteen, wine flask, flat wooden drinking-bottle
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish چوتره (çotra, çotura), ultimately from Ancient Greek κοτύλη (kotúlē).

parole.significato: birdlime, birdglue, a sticky substance smeared on branches to catch birds
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اوكسه (ökse, “birdlime; mistletoe”), from Ancient Greek ἰξός (ixós).
From Ottoman Turkish شماندره (şamandra, şamandara, şamandıra) from Ancient Greek σημαντήρας (sēmantḗras, “buoy”).
